finding.claim: /fetch2 only checks the URL scheme and fetches any http(s) URL, including internal addresses (127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, private ranges), and follows redirects. Full SSRF; the response body (first 200 chars) is returned to the attacker.
finding.sink: requests.get(url, timeout=5) at views.py:22 (allow_redirects defaults to True)

trace.note: urlparse(url).scheme in (http, https); no host or IP check
requests.get follows redirects, body returned in JSON

finding.guards_checked: is_http_url is a scheme check only. There is no host/IP allowlist, no private-range block, and redirects are not disabled.

verdict.guard_found: none (is_http_url at validators.py:7 is a scheme-only check; the stronger is_safe_url is used only by /fetch, not /fetch2)
verdict.reason: views.py:19-22 passes the attacker-supplied `url` query parameter through the scheme-only check at validators.py:7 into requests.get(url, timeout=5) with redirects enabled, and returns the first 200 characters of the body, so internal hosts are reachable.

finding.claim: /fetch validates the hostname by resolving it in is_safe_url, then requests.get resolves it again. An attacker-controlled DNS server can answer with a public IP at check time and 127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254 at connect time (DNS rebinding / TOCTOU). The result is a bypass of the SSRF filter with the response body returned.

trace.note: socket.getaddrinfo resolves the hostname for the check only
requests.get re-resolves the hostname independently; the checked IP is not pinned

finding.guards_checked: allow_redirects=False blocks redirect-based bypass. The scheme check is present. The IP check is not enforced at connect time, so a short-TTL rebinding DNS record defeats it. Also, the check uses parsed.port or 443 while the fetch uses the URL's real port, which is harmless here. The check does not cover IPv4-mapped IPv6 edge cases beyond what ipaddress flags.

verdict.guard_found: none closing: scheme check and getaddrinfo IP denylist at validators.py:12-17 (not pinned to connect), allow_redirects=False at views.py:14; no hostname allowlist
verdict.reason: views.py:11 takes an attacker-controlled url, validators.py:14-16 resolves and checks IPs only at check time, and views.py:14 calls requests.get, which resolves the hostname again without pinning the checked IP, so a rebinding DNS record bypasses the filter and the body is returned.
